oewn-02042493-s.learner: following what is morally right and fair in the way you act.
examples: if you do not tell me in an honourable manner, I shall certainly be reduced to tricks and stratagems to find it out.
with the rich he is liberal-minded, just, sincere, rational, honourable, and, perhaps, agreeable

oewn-14017633-n.learner: being free from the control or influence of another person or of other people.
examples: her husband's love of independence had alone prevented their exceeding their income.
It seems to me to show an abominable sort of conceited independence, a most country-town indifference to decorum.

oewn-07489146-n.learner: the successful end of the American Revolution.
examples: The years after independence were hard for the young United States.
it must very materially lessen their chance of marrying men of any consideration in the world
Miss Bennet's astonishment was soon lessened by the strong sisterly partiality which made any admiration of Elizabeth appear perfectly natural

oewn-00151509-v.learner: to become smaller in size, in how far it reaches, or in how wide it spreads.
examples: The gap between rich and poor lessened over those years.

oewn-00233328-v.learner: to slowly go away, or to become less strong.
examples: By evening the storm had lessened.

oewn-05928866-n.learner: an idea that keeps coming back in a piece of writing or art and helps hold the whole work together.
examples: The motif of the journey runs through the whole novel.

oewn-03794547-n.learner: a design or figure made of shapes or colours that repeat, for example on buildings or in decoration.
examples: The walls were painted with a leaf motif.

oewn-07043169-n.learner: a musical idea that is repeated, or built on and developed, in a piece of music.
examples: The four-note motif comes back again and again in the symphony.

oewn-01590750-a.learner: pleasant or pleasing, in the way something is or in the way it looks.
examples: Mrs. Philips protested that they would have a nice comfortable noisy game of lottery tickets
A low phaeton with a nice little pair of ponies would be the very thing.

oewn-02000490-s.learner: proper by the rules of society or custom; having good taste and manners, or being morally good.
examples: Nice girls did not go to the dances alone in those days.

connotation.why: measures a person against social standards of propriety

oewn-00987524-s.learner: far too fussy and particular, and easily disgusted.
examples: He was so nice about cleanliness that he would not sit on the grass.

connotation.why: calls the fussiness excessive where 'particular' would not

oewn-02170805-v.learner: to look past something, or to fail to notice it.
examples: I overlooked the note on the table and went out without reading it.

oewn-00616690-v.learner: to leave something undone, or to leave something out.
examples: In the rush to leave, they overlooked locking the back door.

oewn-02727841-v.learner: to face in a certain direction.
examples: The front windows overlook the street, and the back ones the fields.

oewn-02701971-v.learner: to look down on something from above.
examples: The castle overlooks the whole valley from its hill.

oewn-02170692-v.learner: to watch over someone or something, keeping an eye on them.
examples: A teacher overlooked the children as they worked.

oewn-06702042-n.learner: approval that lets you do something.
examples: Mr. Denny addressed them directly, and entreated permission to introduce his friend, Mr. Wickham
I have your respected mother's permission for this address.

oewn-01141515-n.learner: the act of formally allowing something, usually in writing.
examples: Planning permission for the new houses was granted by the council last week.

oewn-00005436-r.learner: in a simple way, with nothing too much and nothing added just to decorate.
examples: The room was plainly furnished, with just a bed and a chair.

oewn-02564777-v.learner: to destroy something, or to make it fail.
examples: He had ruined for a while every hope of happiness for the most affectionate, generous heart in the world
You are determined to ruin him in the opinion of all his friends

oewn-01566925-v.learner: to destroy something completely, or to damage it so badly that it can never be fixed.
examples: The flood ruined the carpets beyond repair.

oewn-02323145-v.learner: to make someone lose all their money so that they cannot pay what they owe.
examples: The failed bank ruined thousands of families, who lost all their savings.

oewn-01569271-v.learner: to break a building or place down until only ruins are left.
examples: The bombs ruined the old church, leaving only its walls standing.

oewn-00580070-v.learner: to fall into a broken and wrecked state
examples: Left empty for a hundred years, the old castle slowly ruined.
Her family feared that he had ruined her and would not marry her.

connotation.why: frames loss of virginity as destruction of the person

oewn-01811926-s.learner: strongly disliking something because you have had too much of it.
examples: "I am sick of Mr. Bingley," cried his wife.
The fact is, that you were sick of civility, of deference, of officious attention.

connotation.why: stronger distaste toward the thing than 'tired of'

oewn-02552072-a.learner: having a body or mind that is not working as it normally should; ill.
examples: every possible attention might be paid to the sick lady and her sister.

oewn-02556459-s.learner: feeling as if you are going to vomit.
examples: The rolling of the boat made her feel sick.

oewn-01564558-s.learner: strongly affected by a powerful feeling.
examples: He was sick with worry until the letter came.

oewn-00197276-s.learner: shockingly disgusting, so that it fills people with horror.
examples: He told a sick joke about the accident.

connotation.why: passes moral disgust on the thing, beyond 'gruesome'

oewn-02082451-s.learner: mad; having a mind that is affected by insanity.
examples: Only a sick mind could plan such a crime.

connotation.why: used of a person's mind in place of neutral 'mentally ill'

oewn-02333753-s.learner: (of light) weak and not bright; dim or faint.
examples: A sick yellow light came through the dirty window.
